                                    PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                               SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349



APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                              §
DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                              §                  BEFORE THE
TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION                          §
TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF                             §                 STATE OFFICE
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE                          §
BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL                        §                         OF
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE                        §
PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,                           §               ADMINISTRATIVE
CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,                           §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS,                           §                    HEARINGS
SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                           §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                    §




                                       KEVIN KENNEDY’S

                    EXCEPTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL FOR DECISION

       Kevin Kennedy ("Mr. Kennedy”), a pro se intervenor, respectfully files these Exceptions

to the Proposal for Decision (“PFD”) pursuant to the PUC OPDM memorandum filed on August

20, 2026.

       Mr. Kennedy takes exception to VII.B – The PBRP, under NEED (Issues 5-7) of the

PFD. Specifically, the PFD fails to point out that ERCOT did not use all TSP load demand

information available to them in their PBRP topology model, which was the foundation of their

recommendation for the three import paths. As such, the PBRP does not comply with the

mandates of HB 5066 and it was not performed in compliance with the requirements PURA §

37.056(c-1) and therefore, all that flows from the PBRP is fruit of the poison tree, including the

CCN applications for all five dockets of the PBRP Import Paths.

       Mr. Kennedy also takes exception to VIII.C.1 and VIII.C.1A.




KENNEDY 59475 – Exceptions to Proposal for Decision                                       Page 1 of 6
    I. CLARIFICATIONS TO THE PFD:

           a. Provide additional information in Section VII.B - The PBRP (pp. 58-62)

               PURA § 37.056(c-1) states, “In considering the need for additional service under
               Subsection (c)(2) for a reliability transmission project that serves the ERCOT
               power region or under Subsection (c)(4)(F), the commission must consider the
               historical load, forecasted load growth, and additional load currently seeking
               interconnection, including load for which the electric utility has yet to sign an
               interconnection agreement, as determined by the electric utility with the
               responsibility for serving the load.”


               During calendar year 2024, ERCOT concurrently developed two separate and
               distinct topology models: one for the PBRP and the other for the 2024-RTP. The
               primary difference in the two models, as evidenced by the reports themselves, is
               the load demand input and the resulting future planned generation added to the
               model as necessary to balance with the load demand input. The PBRP only
               considers the new PURA § 37.056(c-1) TSP load demands within the boundary of
               the Permian Basin, and excludes consideration of the much larger remainder of
               the new PURA § 37.056(c-1) TSP load demands that fall outside of the Permian
               Basin.


               This fact is evidenced by the 17,170-MW of planned generation including in the
               PBRP model, as provided in PBRP Appendix A.1. This is the amount of future
               generation added to offset any demand in the PBRP that could not be met by
               existing generation facilities.


               In the PBRP (p. iii), ERCOT states, “ERCOT also anticipates significant load
               growth outside the Permian Basin region. TDSP load forecasts for the 2024
               Regional Transmission Plan (RTP) have identified approximately 59,400 MW of
               additional demand across the ERCOT System that will need to be served by
               2030.” This load demand would need to be offset by future planned generation in
               the 2024-RTP model. 2024-RTP, Appendix B provides the validation we seek,


KENNEDY 59475 – Exceptions to Proposal for Decision                                        Page 2 of 6
                documenting that it was necessary to add 59,202-MW of future planned
               generation to offset the full accounting of all new PURA § 37.056(c-1) TSP load
               demands.


               The 42,000-MW difference between the future planned generation needed in the
               two models, documents the magnitude of the significant difference in the future
               load demand inputs ERCOT used in the models. If the two models had the same
               forecasted load demand, they would also have the same future planned
               generation. For unknown reasons, ERCOT did not consider all new PURA §
               37.056(c-1) TSP load demands in the PBRP; leaving out approximately 42,000-
               MW of known forecasted demand. This not only violates PURA requirements,
               but it would almost certainly lead to erroneous and untrustworthy results, and
               recommendations from the PBRP.


               ERCOT does not have the authority to reduce or ignore known, forecasted load
               demand when developing reliability plans. The fact they do not have authority is
               reinforced by ERCOT’s Request for Good Cause Exception to adjust TSP loads
               for the 2025-RTP (55999-121). By this request, which was submitted one week
               after the PUC Commissioners approved ERCOT’s PBRP 765-kV import strategy,
               ERCOT admits only the PUC and the Legislature can reduce load demand
               forecasts submitted by TSPs, as required by PURA § 37.056(c-1).


               In Oncor’s Response to ERCOT’s Request for Good Cause Exception (55999-
               125), the argument ERCOT does not have authority to not consider TSP load
               demand is furthered when Oncor states, “Oncor is concerned that ERCOT’s
               proposed methodology, which seeks to greatly discount Transmission and/or
               Distribution Service Provider (“TDSP”) officer letter attested load values used in
               the 2025 Regional Transmission Plan (“RTP”) base cases, is contrary to clear
               statutory direction. Both S.B. 1281 and H.B. 5066 manifest the Legislature’s clear
               intent that the Public Utility Commission of Texas (the “Commission”) defer to
               TDSPs’ load forecasts when evaluating utility projects in CCN proceedings.”




KENNEDY 59475 – Exceptions to Proposal for Decision                                     Page 3 of 6
                I could not have said it better myself. ERCOT is statutorily required to consider
               (include) all TSP load forecasts but they arbitrarily ignored a staggering 42,000-
               MW of known TSP load forecasts outside the Permian Basin when developing
               their PBRP modeling, analysis, and recommendations.

               By excluding consideration of approximately 42,000-MW of new TSP load
               growth outside the Permian, they modeled a 2030 and 2038 demand condition
               that would never exist in the real world. The erroneous load demand would cause
               any person to reasonably assume the model was flawed; therefore, ERCOT’s
               consequential import path recommendations would likewise be assumed a fallacy.

               Not only should ERCOT’s PBRP not be given “great weight” but it should be
               considered a flawed and statutorily invalid study and everything that flows from it
               should be consider fruit of the poison tree, including all five PBRP import path
               CCN dockets that relied solely on the PBRP for justification of need, those being
               PUC Dockets 59029, 59182, 59315, 59336, and 59475.

           b. Revise VIII.C.1 Florence Elementary School (p. 109)

               The Proposal for Decision states, “The Application erroneously identified the
               school as a habitable structure, when it should have also been identified as an
               elementary school.”

               Mr. Kennedy respectfully requests that this sentence be revised as follows:
               “The Application erroneously identified the school as a Commercial / Industrial
               habitable structure, when it should have been identified as an Elementary School
               habitable structure.”

               The Applicants did not simply fail to label the school; they described the school
               as a commercial / industrial site. This distinction must be made known to the
               Commission as it is indicative of the overall lack of quality and lack of accuracy
               of the application. The Applicants also identified two churches as commercial /
               industrial sites. The Applicants identified deer camp travel trailers as habitable
               “structures”. These and many other questionable items in the application, which


KENNEDY 59475 – Exceptions to Proposal for Decision                                        Page 4 of 6
                could dramatically affect route evaluation, beg the question of whether the
               application can be relied upon to identify a recommended route. The Commission
               must be aware of these deficiencies.


           c. Add new section VIII.C.1X Churches (~ p. 112)


               The Applicants erroneously identified two churches as commercial / industrial
               sites in their in the Application. One of the misidentified churches was on a route
               added after the public meeting and was afforded little time to participate in the
               process and provide data to the Applicants. This information is important as it
               goes to not only the lack of accuracy and quality of the Application in its entirety,
               but it reinforces the need for meaningful opportunity of public participation.


               The Applicants have an obligation to provide a reasonable standard of care
               regarding all aspects of an application to amend a CCN. The ALJs, Commission,
               landowners and rate payers must be able to rely on the accuracy and completeness
               of the data collected and presented by the Applicants. When that standard of care
               is not met, the Commission has no reliable or trustworthy basis for selecting a
               route.


   II. REVISED FINDINGS OF FACTS
               Need for Import Path 2

               XX.      PURA § 37.056(c-1) requires all future TSP load demands must be
               considered in development of reliability plans.


               XX.      For the PBRP, ERCOT did not consider approximately 42,000-MW of
               future TSP load demands, which was located outside the Permian Basin.


               XX.      The results and recommendations from ERCOT’s PBRP are erroneous due
               to ERCOT’s failure to properly consider the effects of all forecasted load demand
               within the ERCOT grid, and the impacts those future load demands would have
               on future transmission needs.


KENNEDY 59475 – Exceptions to Proposal for Decision                                        Page 5 of 6
       III. CONCLUSIONS OF LAW

                 XX.     ERCOT’s PBRP did not comply with the statutory requirements of PURA
                         § 37.056(c-1) and is therefore, invalid for use as CCN need justification.



      IV. PRAYER

         Mr. Kennedy does not present any new information into the evidentiary record. Both the

      PBRP and the 2024-RTP are already exhibits in the record. He simply shines disinfecting

      sunlight on existing evidence not previously viewed under this brighter light of statutory

      scrutiny. Mr. Kennedy y’all ALJs will fully contemplate the overall ramifications of

      ERCOT’s actions and render true and just modifications to their Proposal for Decision.



Date Signed: September 2, 2026



Respectfully submitted,

Kevin Kennedy


By:      /s/ J. Kevin Kennedy



630 County Road 282

Bertram, Texas 78605

Telephone: (512) 639-1720

Email: jkkennedy.tx@gmail.com
